disease_label_per_paper: Probable donor-derived human adenovirus type 34 infection with tubulointerstitial nephritis in a kidney transplant recipient
presentation_summary: 36-year-old man developed symptoms one month after deceased donor kidney transplant for end-stage renal disease.
He presented with three days of allograft tenderness, hematuria, fever, dysuria, and urinary retention while receiving tacrolimus, mycophenolate, prednisone, and antimicrobial prophylaxis.

Admission evaluation showed low-grade fever, hemodynamic stability, allograft tenderness, WBC 5.9 x10^9/L with lymphopenia, hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL, platelets 166 x10^9/L, and creatinine 1.69 mg/dL above baseline.
Urine contained many RBCs and WBCs, and abdominal CT showed perinephric stranding consistent with allograft pyelonephritis.
On hospital day 3 he worsened with allograft tenderness and fever to 40 C; cultures were negative; serum adenovirus PCR and biopsy confirmed adenovirus type 34 allograft infection.
